author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
I am screening resumes lately, I found many students are hiding the fact that they code with AI in their github repo by putting CLAUDE.md in gitignore.
Are the school still teach using AI to write code equals cheating these days?
I would know more about whether the student is a good programmer by looking at the commit history of CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md

author.name: James Carlson
author.headline: Computer Information Science student at Washburn University

comments.text: Yeah, I saw a person who is a software engineer who had 5 projects in his GitHub repo all of which had 3-4 commits and on 3 of his projects he had these HUGE 200 line .gitignore files with comments that included Claude.md, and one of his projects didn't even have a README. I really like problem solving through these things but I feel like I'm being left behind by people who just use AI to make everything for themselves. I use AI for my projects but I only make it act like a senior developer and make sure that I am not copying code and redirecting it to not give me code if it does gives me code.

author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

replies.text: James Carlson if you hide CLAUDE.md, other people can't fork your repo and make changes using AI.

author.name: Chadi Jmai
author.headline: Engineering the Future: Driven by Ambition and Innovation

comments.text: I think it goes beyond what schools teach. Students often want to use AI, but they also want full credit for the outcome. That creates a tension around authorship: when does AI-supported work still count as "my work"? That question is probably more useful than simply asking whether AI use is cheating

author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

replies.text: Chadi Jmai I use AI to write 200% of my code (yeah, I have to delete half of the sloppy code) Those code are all my code. In fact I even check in the chat session so my instructions that I have to AI is in the record history
